newsitem.title: USA: DC control board rejects mayor's FY98 draft budget.
newsitem.headline: DC control board rejects mayor's FY98 draft budget.

text.p: The District of Columbia financial control board rejected Mayor Marion Barry's draft fiscal 1998 budget saying it does not provide enough funds for public safety and schools.
The five-member panel on Monday, headed by economist Andrew Brimmer, gave the city 15 days to overhaul the plan, which the control board must approve and send to Capitol Hill by June 15.

Brimmer said Barry's plan would cut overall spending for public safety by $41.8 million. And while funding for police would rise by $7.2 million, that still leaves a "very large gap" in what that department needs to do its job, Brimmer said. He added expressed concern that the city's corrections department also would be cut by $20.3 million.

The control board's chief said that while Barry's budget would fund 3,800 uniformed officers, it includes no pay raise. A raise is "defenitely necessary" to keep police from joining suburban police departments, he said. Brimmer complained that Barry's plan also would cut public school spending by $28.3 million, or 4.9 percent, at a time when public school trustees are calling for a 7.2 percent increase in fiscal 1998.
"I believe the schools should have an increase in their budget," Brimmer said, adding, however, that he does not back the full 7.2 percent hike.

Brimmer said Barry also should seek more dollars for a large backlog of school construction and renovations. Barry said he is not surprised that the board rejected the budget. He said he and D.C. chief financial officer Anthony Williams are "steadfastly working" on revisions.

Barry added, however, that "philosophical differences" beterween the mayor and control board will continue. "There are certain programs and policies that I will continue to fight for because I am elected by the people of the District to represent their interests," Barry said.
